601.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
601.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

601.clozeText: Living in the countryside offers many wonderful advantages. Firstly, the atmosphere is fresh and clean because there are not many (23) ________ on the roads. People can enjoy the peaceful nature with green paddy fields and tranquil rivers. Secondly, the villagers are extremely (24) ________ and willing to support each other. Food in rural areas is usually fresh and (25) ________ than food in big cities. However, there are (26) ________ shopping malls or entertainment centers. Many young people still prefer (27) ________ in cities for better job opportunities.
601.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐỌC HIỂU (READING COMPREHENSION - PART 5):
Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

602.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
602.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

602.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

603.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
603.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

Many young people still prefer (27) ________ in cities for better job opportunities.
603.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

604.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
604.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

604.clozeText: Living in the countryside offers many wonderful advantages. Firstly, the atmosphere is fresh and clean because there are not many (23) ________ on the roads. People can enjoy the peaceful nature with green paddy fields and tranquil rivers. Secondly, the villagers are extremely (24) ________ and willing to support each other. Food in rural areas is usually fresh and (25) ________ than food in big cities. However, there are (26) ________ shopping malls or entertainment centers. Many young people still prefer (27) ________ in cities for better job opportunities.
604.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

605.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
605.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

605.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

Living in the countryside offers many wonderful advantages. Firstly, the atmosphere is fresh and clean because there are not many (23) ________ on the roads. People can enjoy the peaceful nature with green paddy fields and tranquil rivers. Secondly, the villagers are extremely (24) ________ and willing to support each other. 📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐỌC HIỂU (READING COMPREHENSION - PART 5):
Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. === PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

606.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. 607.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

607.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

608.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
608.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

Many young people still prefer (27) ________ in cities for better job opportunities.
608.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

609.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
609.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

609.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

610.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
610.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. 611.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
611.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

611.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

612.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
612.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

612.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

613.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
613.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

613.clozeText: Living in the countryside offers many wonderful advantages. Firstly, the atmosphere is fresh and clean because there are not many (23) ________ on the roads. People can enjoy the peaceful nature with green paddy fields and tranquil rivers. Secondly, the villagers are extremely (24) ________ and willing to support each other. Food in rural areas is usually fresh and (25) ________ than food in big cities. However, there are (26) ________ shopping malls or entertainment centers. Many young people still prefer (27) ________ in cities for better job opportunities.
613.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

614.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

614.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

615.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
615.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

615.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

616.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

616.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

617.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
617.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

617.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

618.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
618.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

618.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

619.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 6
619.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.
619.clozeText: Living in the countryside offers many wonderful advantages. Firstly, the atmosphere is fresh and clean because there are not many (23) ________ on the roads. People can enjoy the peaceful nature with green paddy fields and tranquil rivers. Secondly, the villagers are extremely (24) ________ and willing to support each other. Food in rural areas is usually fresh and (25) ________ than food in big cities. However, there are (26) ________ shopping malls or entertainment centers. Many young people still prefer (27) ________ in cities for better job opportunities.
619.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

Food in rural areas is usually fresh and (25) ________ than food in big cities. However, there are (26) ________ shopping malls or entertainment centers. Many young people still prefer (27) ________ in cities for better job opportunities.

📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐỌC HIỂU (READING COMPREHENSION - PART 5):
Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

620.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Linh:: Are you preparing for Tet holiday with your family, Tom?
Tom:: Yes, we are cleaning the house and decorating the peach blossoms.
Linh:: What traditional food do you like most during Tet?
Tom:: I love Chung cake and spring rolls. They are delicious!
Linh:: Children usually receive lucky money in red envelopes, right?
Tom:: Exactly! We wear new clothes and wish our grandparents good health.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Ha Long Bay is one of the most famous natural wonders in Viet Nam. It is situated in Quang Ninh Province. The bay consists of thousands of magnificent limestone islands and mysterious caves such as Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. Tourists can enjoy a boat cruise around the emerald water, kayak into caves, or swim at beautiful sandy beaches. Visitors must preserve the natural environment and mustn't litter into the sea.

620.readingText: Tet is the most important traditional festival for Vietnamese people. It usually occurs in late January or early February. Before Tet, people thoroughly clean and decorate their homes with apricot blossoms in the South or peach blossoms in the North. Families gather to make square Chung cakes, which symbolize the Earth. On New Year's Day, people wear nice clothes and visit temples to pray for luck and happiness. Children receive red envelopes containing lucky money from elders. Everyone avoids saying unpleasant things to ensure good fortune throughout the whole year.

701.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
701.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

702.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
702.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

703.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
703.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

704.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
704.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

705.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
705.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

706.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

707.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
707.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

708.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
708.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

709.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
709.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

710.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

711.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
711.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

712.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
712.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

713.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

714.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
714.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

715.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
715.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

716.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
716.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

717.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
717.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

718.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

719.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

720.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 7
720.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nick:: Have you ever visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, Mai?
Mai:: Yes, I visited it last summer with my classmates and history teacher.
Nick:: What is its special historical significance?
Mai:: It was founded in 1070 and became Viet Nam's first national university in 1076.
Nick:: What can visitors see there today?
Mai:: There are ancient pavilions, the Well of Heavenly Clarity, and 82 stone doctor tablets.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Vietnamese culinary culture is globally celebrated for its harmonious balance of flavors, fresh ingredients, and low fat content. Among various traditional specialties, Pho' stands out as the national signature dish. A fragrant bowl of beef or chicken Pho features tender rice noodles, sliced meat, and a simmered broth seasoned with cinnamon, star anise, and roasted ginger. Pho is typically served hot with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and a pinch of chili.

801.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
801.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

801.clozeText: Terraced rice fields in northern Viet Nam's mountainous highlands represent a masterclass in indigenous agricultural ingenuity and ecological harmony. For centuries, ethnic minority communities such as the HMong, Dao, and Tay have carved cascading agricultural terraces into steep mountainsides. These sculpted landscapes not only maximize arable terrain but also efficiently channel rainwater down slopes without causing severe soil (23) ________. In autumn, particularly in Mu Cang Chai and Hoang Su Phi, the terraced valleys transform into mesmerizing (24) ________ ribbons of golden ripe rice. Thousands of domestic and international travelers trek along rugged trails to capture these breathtaking vistas. Beyond their visual splendor, the terraced fields embody centuries of communal (25) ________, agricultural wisdom, and profound spiritual reverence for Mother (26) ________. The preservation of these heritage landscapes requires sustainable tourism practices that directly empower local indigenous (27) ________.
801.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. For instance, the Ede and Gia Rai in the Central Highlands maintain matriarchal family traditions where lineage and property are inherited through daughters, and weddings are held in elongated wooden longhouses. Conversely, northern highland groups like the HMong and Dao showcase elaborate indigo-dyed hemp costumes adorned with intricate silver embroidery. Preserving this ethnic diversity is a national priority, fostering mutual respect, cultural enrichment, and sustainable socio-economic development across all regions of the fatherland.

802.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
802.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

802.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. 803.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
803.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

803.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. For instance, the Ede and Gia Rai in the Central Highlands maintain matriarchal family traditions where lineage and property are inherited through daughters, and weddings are held in elongated wooden longhouses. Conversely, northern highland groups like the HMong and Dao showcase elaborate indigo-dyed hemp costumes adorned with intricate silver embroidery. Preserving this ethnic diversity is a national priority, fostering mutual respect, cultural enrichment, and sustainable socio-economic development across all regions of the fatherland.

804.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
804.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

804.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. For instance, the Ede and Gia Rai in the Central Highlands maintain matriarchal family traditions where lineage and property are inherited through daughters, and weddings are held in elongated wooden longhouses. Conversely, northern highland groups like the HMong and Dao showcase elaborate indigo-dyed hemp costumes adorned with intricate silver embroidery. Preserving this ethnic diversity is a national priority, fostering mutual respect, cultural enrichment, and sustainable socio-economic development across all regions of the fatherland.

805.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
805.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

805.clozeText: Terraced rice fields in northern Viet Nam's mountainous highlands represent a masterclass in indigenous agricultural ingenuity and ecological harmony. For centuries, ethnic minority communities such as the HMong, Dao, and Tay have carved cascading agricultural terraces into steep mountainsides. These sculpted landscapes not only maximize arable terrain but also efficiently channel rainwater down slopes without causing severe soil (23) ________. In autumn, particularly in Mu Cang Chai and Hoang Su Phi, the terraced valleys transform into mesmerizing (24) ________ ribbons of golden ripe rice. Thousands of domestic and international travelers trek along rugged trails to capture these breathtaking vistas. 805.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. For instance, the Ede and Gia Rai in the Central Highlands maintain matriarchal family traditions where lineage and property are inherited through daughters, and weddings are held in elongated wooden longhouses. 806.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
806.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

806.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. For instance, the Ede and Gia Rai in the Central Highlands maintain matriarchal family traditions where lineage and property are inherited through daughters, and weddings are held in elongated wooden longhouses. Conversely, northern highland groups like the HMong and Dao showcase elaborate indigo-dyed hemp costumes adorned with intricate silver embroidery. Preserving this ethnic diversity is a national priority, fostering mutual respect, cultural enrichment, and sustainable socio-economic development across all regions of the fatherland.

807.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
807.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

807.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. For instance, the Ede and Gia Rai in the Central Highlands maintain matriarchal family traditions where lineage and property are inherited through daughters, and weddings are held in elongated wooden longhouses. Conversely, northern highland groups like the HMong and Dao showcase elaborate indigo-dyed hemp costumes adorned with intricate silver embroidery. Preserving this ethnic diversity is a national priority, fostering mutual respect, cultural enrichment, and sustainable socio-economic development across all regions of the fatherland.

808.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
808.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

Thousands of domestic and international travelers trek along rugged trails to capture these breathtaking vistas. Beyond their visual splendor, the terraced fields embody centuries of communal (25) ________, agricultural wisdom, and profound spiritual reverence for Mother (26) ________. 808.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. For instance, the Ede and Gia Rai in the Central Highlands maintain matriarchal family traditions where lineage and property are inherited through daughters, and weddings are held in elongated wooden longhouses. Conversely, northern highland groups like the HMong and Dao showcase elaborate indigo-dyed hemp costumes adorned with intricate silver embroidery. Preserving this ethnic diversity is a national priority, fostering mutual respect, cultural enrichment, and sustainable socio-economic development across all regions of the fatherland.

Preserving this ethnic diversity is a national priority, fostering mutual respect, cultural enrichment, and sustainable socio-economic development across all regions of the fatherland.

809.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
809.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

809.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. For instance, the Ede and Gia Rai in the Central Highlands maintain matriarchal family traditions where lineage and property are inherited through daughters, and weddings are held in elongated wooden longhouses. Conversely, northern highland groups like the HMong and Dao showcase elaborate indigo-dyed hemp costumes adorned with intricate silver embroidery. Preserving this ethnic diversity is a national priority, fostering mutual respect, cultural enrichment, and sustainable socio-economic development across all regions of the fatherland.

810.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
810.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

810.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. For instance, the Ede and Gia Rai in the Central Highlands maintain matriarchal family traditions where lineage and property are inherited through daughters, and weddings are held in elongated wooden longhouses. Conversely, northern highland groups like the HMong and Dao showcase elaborate indigo-dyed hemp costumes adorned with intricate silver embroidery. Preserving this ethnic diversity is a national priority, fostering mutual respect, cultural enrichment, and sustainable socio-economic development across all regions of the fatherland.

811.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ I - LỚP 8
811.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
David:: How many ethnic groups live in Viet Nam, Linh?
Linh:: There are 54 distinct ethnic groups, with the Kinh people accounting for about 85% of the total population.
David:: Where do most ethnic minorities predominantly reside?
Linh:: They mostly live in mountainous northern provinces and the Central Highlands.
David:: What is unique about the Central Highlands' communal architecture?
Linh:: The majestic Rong house (communal stilt house) with its axe-blade roof serves as the civic and cultural heart of each village.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
In Vietnamese culture, filial piety and ancestor veneration represent the foundational moral pillars of every family. In every Vietnamese household, an ancestor altar is respectfully placed in the most solemn and prominent area of the home. On significant occasions such as New Year celebrations, the death anniversaries of forebears, or full moon days, family descendants gather reverently to burn incense, offer fresh flowers and fruits, and pray for familial peace and prosperity. This deep-rooted tradition honors ancestral roots and reinforces family unity across generations.

811.readingText: The 54 ethnic groups of Viet Nam constitute a vibrant mosaic of cultural heritage, languages, and traditional customs. While the Kinh comprise the vast majority, the remaining 53 ethnic minorities preserve distinctive cultural identities manifested in their folklore, textile craftsmanship, festive ceremonies, and architectural styles. For instance, the Ede and Gia Rai in the Central Highlands maintain matriarchal family traditions where lineage and property are inherited through daughters, and weddings are held in elongated wooden longhouses. Conversely, northern highland groups like the HMong and Dao showcase elaborate indigo-dyed hemp costumes adorned with intricate silver embroidery. Preserving this ethnic diversity is a national priority, fostering mutual respect, cultural enrichment, and sustainable socio-economic development across all regions of the fatherland.
